paper.title_en: Geodesic congruences and stability of spacetimes with specifically warped extra dimension
paper.abstract_en: In this work, we investigate timelike geodesic congruences in the background of two non singular, asymptotically flat spacetimes with a specifically warped extra dimension. The stability of these geometries under the propagation of a massive scalar field is also analyzed. The expansion, shear and rotation (ESR) analysis shows that geodesic congruences are irrotational, with expansion and shear vanishing asymptotically both in the presence and absence of extra-dimensional effect. A detailed study of caustic formation is carried out for both geometries, revealing that the congruences undergo progressive contraction and distortion as they evolve from the asymptotic region toward the caustic. The scalar field experiences a single barrier and a double barrier effective potential in the first and second types of spacetime geometries respectively. In the case of the double barrier potential, multiple reflections of the scalar field between the two peaks give rise to an initial ringdown phase followed by echoes. These echoes gradually decay over time, eventually leading to a late time ringing phase that dominates the signal. The WKB method is employed to compute the quasinormal frequencies (QNFs) for single barrier potentials; however, it is not suitable for the double barrier case. To address this limitation and to validate the WKB results, the Prony fitting method is utilized to determine the QNFs. The influence of various geometric parameters on the QNFs is also examined. The analysis shows that the QNFs possess both real and imaginary components, with the negative imaginary part indicating the stability of the spacetimes under scalar field perturbation.
